summary.text: The Great Oxidation Event was the stretch of time when free oxygen first rose in Earth's air and shallow seas, from about 2.46–2.426 billion years ago to around 2.06 billion years ago.
It is inferred to have been caused by cyanobacteria, whose photosynthesis releases oxygen as a byproduct of splitting water.
Free oxygen was toxic to the mostly anaerobic life of the time and may have caused many early organisms to die out.

facts.label: Other names
facts.value: Oxygen Catastrophe, Oxygen Revolution, Oxygen Crisis

facts.label: Oxygen by the end
facts.value: Up to 10% of the modern level

facts.label: Biosphere shrinkage
facts.value: Interpreted as over 80% at the end

items.prompt: Riverbed sediments older than about 2.4 billion years hold grains of pyrite and uraninite, minerals that only last when oxygen is scarce. What do they reveal?

options.label: The air then was rich in oxygen
The atmosphere then was anoxic
Rivers then flowed much faster
The grains fell in as meteorites

items.explain: Because these minerals are stable only under low oxygen, finding them as worn grains in river and delta sediments points to an anoxic atmosphere.

items.prompt: A geologist finds a red sandstone coated with hematite. What does its color say about the conditions when it formed?

options.label: It settled in deep, airless water
A volcano baked it until red
It is packed with organic matter
Enough oxygen was around to oxidize iron

items.explain: Red beds show there was enough oxygen to turn iron into its ferric state, unlike sandstones laid down without oxygen, which are often beige, white, grey or green.

items.prompt: What living things are thought to have triggered this rise in oxygen?

options.label: Cyanobacteria
Early land plants
The first animals
Methane-making microbes

items.explain: Cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis that releases oxygen as a byproduct, and they are inferred to have caused the event.

items.prompt: Banded iron formations need iron carried in solution through the ocean. Why did they largely stop forming around 1.85 billion years ago?

options.label: Earth's crust ran short of it
Seawater grew too cold
The deep ocean became oxygenated
Volcanoes stopped erupting

items.explain: An oxygenated ocean turns the iron into insoluble ferric compounds before it can be carried to basins, so the end of these deposits marks deep-ocean oxygenation.

items.prompt: Why was the newly abundant free oxygen deadly to many microbes of the time?

options.label: It blocked sunlight from reaching them
It oxidizes organic compounds like genes
It made the seawater far too salty
It raised the sea temperature sharply

items.explain: Free oxygen is highly reactive and can oxidize organic compounds, especially genetic material, which made it toxic to the mostly anaerobic life.

items.prompt: Dark, finely layered shale rich in organic matter is often taken as a sign of low oxygen. Why is it a poor sign on its own for rocks of this age?

options.label: Such shale only ever forms on land
Its dark color fades over time
Rock that old can never be dated
Burrowers that mix layers hadn't evolved

items.explain: Organic-rich deposits don't prove anoxia, and burrowing creatures that would destroy the layering did not yet exist, so the layers would survive either way.
